_note: Published name forms, keyed by kind/slug. Every entry names its source. The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India is published directly as the statutory reference; anything from Wikidata appears only where an independent named source corroborated it, and `rejected` records what was thrown out. Regenerate with scripts/apply-names.mjs; do not hand-edit.

rejected.name: चांगेरी
rejected.denotesInstead: Correct species (Oxalis corniculata) but wrong language: चांगेरी is the SANSKRIT name, not Hindi.
rejected.reason: This is the batch's real error. Two independent sources agree on the language assignment and both contradict the candidate. Flowers of India ('Creeping Wood Sorrel', Oxalis corniculata) lists "Sanskrit: चांगेरी Changeri, अम्लः Amla, अम्ली Amli" and separately "Hindi: Amrul अम्रुल" — चांगेरी appears under Sanskrit, Marathi and Kannada, never Hindi. The Kerala State Medicinal Plants Board herbal database (smpbkerala.in) independently gives Sanskrit "Changeri", Hindi "Amrul", Tamil "Puliyarai". So the name is genuine and the species is right, but filed in the wrong language slot, which on a published monograph would misinform every Hindi reader. The Hindi name is अम्रुल.

rejected.name: क्षीरिणीसस्यम्
rejected.denotesInstead: Manilkara hexandra (syn. Mimusops hexandra); and as Satyanāśī, Argemone mexicana — both given for क्षीरिणी in nighantu literature
rejected.reason: Two separate problems. First, the form: no source attests क्षीरिणीसस्यम्. Flowers of India gives Sanskrit "अनंतमूल Anantamul, Sariva" for H. indicus and MMPND gives "Anantamoola, Sariva" — neither mentions Kṣīriṇī, and the -सस्यम् suffix is the Sanskrit Wikipedia pattern. Second, and worse, the base word is not species-specific: wisdomlib's Kṣīriṇī entry records it as a name of Manilkara hexandra (Sapotaceae) and, as Satyanāśī, of Argemone mexicana / Euphorbia spp., and the Rāja Nighaṇṭu lists Kṣīriṇī as an unidentified plant. It does carry a secondary modern application to Hemidesmus, so it is ambiguous rather than flatly wrong — but ambiguous is disqualifying for a headline Sanskrit name on a botanical reference. Use सारिवा or अनन्तमूला.

rejected.name: अश्वत्थः
rejected.denotesInstead: Ficus religiosa L. (the peepal / sacred fig)
rejected.reason: This is the planted error. Monier-Williams p.115, quoted in the Pandanus record for Ficus religiosa: "aśvattha, as, m. (ttha-stha, 'under which horses stand') the holy fig tree, Ficus Religiosa, AV.; ŚBr." API Vol I has a whole monograph titled AŚVATTHA whose botanical source is Ficus religiosa Linn. Pandanus lists aśvattha as one of only two Sanskrit names for Ficus religiosa (with pippala), and does not list it under Terminalia arjuna at all. Terminalia arjuna's Sanskrit names are अर्जुनः and ककुभः. This is a genuine Sanskrit tree name attached to the wrong species and would mislead a reader if it survived on the page.

rejected.name: வெண் மருது
rejected.denotesInstead: Terminalia paniculata Roth (per Tamil Lexicon); the Tamil names for T. arjuna are நீர்மருது and வெள்ளைமருது
rejected.reason: Tamil Lexicon p.3782 glosses "வெண்மருது veṇ-marutu, n. பூமருது, 1." and p.2840 gives "பூமருது pū-marutu, n. Terminalia paniculata" for sense 1 — so the Lexicon assigns வெண்மருது to Terminalia paniculata, not to arjuna. The Lexicon reserves arjuna for other headwords: p.2306 "நீர்மருது nīr-marutu, n. Arjuna, Terminalia arjuna" and p.3803 "வெள்ளைமருது veḷḷai-marutu, n. பூமருது, 1. 2. Arjuna. See நீர்மருது". Pandanus lists veṇmarutu only under MALAYALAM for T. arjuna; its Tamil list is āṟṟumarutu, nīrmarutu, veḷḷaimarutu, marutu. API Vol II gives Tamil: Marudam. A contested modern usage exists (Tamil Wikipedia titles the species வெண்மருது), which is very likely the Wikidata source, but the dictionary referent is a different Terminalia.

rejected.name: अश्वत्थः
rejected.denotesInstead: Ficus religiosa L. (the peepal / sacred fig)
rejected.reason: The planted error again, on the second Terminalia arjuna page. Monier-Williams p.115: aśvattha = "the holy fig tree, Ficus Religiosa"; API Vol I monograph AŚVATTHA is sourced from Ficus religiosa Linn; Pandanus gives aśvattha and pippala as the two Sanskrit names of Ficus religiosa. It is not a name for Terminalia arjuna in any source retrieved, and must not appear on an Arjuna Twak page.

rejected.name: வெண் மருது
rejected.denotesInstead: Terminalia paniculata Roth (per Tamil Lexicon); T. arjuna is நீர்மருது / வெள்ளைமருது
rejected.reason: Same as [arjuna]: Tamil Lexicon p.3782 equates வெண்மருது with பூமருது sense 1, and p.2840 gives பூமருது = Terminalia paniculata. The Lexicon's arjuna entries are நீர்மருது (p.2306) and வெள்ளைமருது (p.3803). API Vol II gives Tamil Marudam. Pandanus places veṇmarutu in Malayalam, not Tamil, for this species.

rejected.name: अश्वत्थः
rejected.denotesInstead: Ficus religiosa L. (the peepal / sacred fig)
rejected.reason: The planted error, third occurrence in this batch. Monier-Williams p.115: "aśvattha, as, m. ... the holy fig tree, Ficus Religiosa, AV.; ŚBr."; API Vol I has a monograph AŚVATTHA sourced from Ficus religiosa Linn; Pandanus gives the Sanskrit names of Ficus religiosa as pippala and aśvattha. Saraca asoca's Sanskrit names are अशोकः and कङ्केलिः (Monier-Williams p.113, API Vol I). Aśvattha has no connection to Saraca and must be removed.

rejected.name: सन
rejected.denotesInstead: Crotalaria juncea L. (sunn hemp)
rejected.reason: A real Hindi plant name attached to the wrong species. MMPND Sorting Crotalaria lists under Crotalaria juncea: HINDI सन San, सनई Sannai, सऩ Sunn, Kharif, and SANSKRIT शणपुष्पी Śaṇapuṣpī — the English names given there are Sunn hemp, San hemp, Bengal hemp. For Linum usitatissimum, neither MMPND (which lists no Hindi at all for the species) nor API Vol I (Hindi: Alsi) nor Platts (अलसी, तीसी) gives सन. The confusion is intelligible — both are fibre crops — but सन on a flax page is a botanical error, since it points to a legume in a different family.

rejected.name: कृष्णखदिरवृक्षः
rejected.denotesInstead: reads literally as a name for Acacia catechu — खदिर is Acacia catechu per API Vol I, monograph KHADIRA (Hindi: Khair, Tamil: Karungali), not Acacia nilotica
rejected.reason: Unattested, and actively misleading. Wisdomlib has no entry for krishnakhadira (404). The Sanskrit names actually retrieved for this species: API Vol I BABBŪLA gives Bāvarī and Kinkirāta; Pandanus gives barbura and babbūla; Monier-Williams and Apte give babbula/babbūla and varvūra. Meanwhile खदिर is a different pharmacopoeial drug entirely — API Vol I has a separate KHADIRA monograph from Acacia catechu, Hindi Khair, English 'Black catechu, Cutch tree'. So a compound built on खदिर and prefixed कृष्ण- ('black') points a reader at Acacia catechu. MMPND does record a comparable descriptive string, 'Kala barbura vrikshaha', under A. nilotica subsp. subalata, which shows how such coinages arise, but that is built on बर्बुर, not खदिर.

rejected.name: पङ्क्तिः
rejected.denotesInstead: not a plant at all — Sanskrit for 'a line, row, series'; in Ayurvedic plant morphology paṅkti / paṅktivallarī is one of the eight types of inflorescence (vallarī)
rejected.reason: The clearest pure artifact in the batch. Checked the wisdomlib entry for 'pankti': the word means a line, row or series, a group or assembly; the only botanical use is as Paṅktivallarī, a named type of flower arrangement in which floral parts are set in rows. No source identifies it as a plant species, and none of API Vol I (Bāvarī, Kinkirāta), Pandanus (barbura, babbūla) or Monier-Williams lists it under Acacia nilotica. This looks like a morphology term or a table label scraped out of context; it should be deleted.

rejected.name: சித்தாமுட்டி
rejected.denotesInstead: Pavonia glechomifolia and Pavonia zeylanica per Tamil Lexicon (contested: MMPND lists 'Chitaamuttie' for Sida cordifolia)
rejected.reason: The Tamil Lexicon routes this name to a different genus. p.1412: "சித்தாமுட்டி cittāmuṭṭi, n. [K. ciṭṭāmuṭṭi.] See சிற்றாமுட்டி. Colloq.", and p.1452: "சிற்றாமுட்டி ciṟṟā-muṭṭi, n. முட்டி. 1. Yellow sticky mallow, s. sh., Pavonia glechomifolia; 2. Rose-coloured sticky mallow, s. sh., Pavonia zeylanica". The Lexicon's own name for this page's species is different again — a full-text search for 'Sida cordifolia' returns exactly one entry, p.2274: "நிலத்துத்தி nila-t-tutti, n. Downy heart-leaved morning mallow, s. sh., Sida cordifolia" — and IISc's India Flora Online herbsheet for Sida cordifolia gives Tamil 'Nilatutti' only. MMPND Sorting Sida does list TAMIL: Chitaamuttie under Sida cordifolia, so the attribution is contested rather than baseless, but with the University of Madras Lexicon and IISc both against it and both naming நிலத்துத்தி instead, this should not go on the page unqualified. Both genera are Malvaceae 'mallows', which is how the confusion propagates.

rejected.name: பூளை
rejected.denotesInstead: Aerva javanica (Burm.f.) Juss. ex Schult. per Tamil Lexicon sense 3; in sense 1 the same headword means red silk-cotton, இலவு / Bombax ceiba
rejected.reason: The bare form names the wrong Aerva. Tamil Lexicon p.2853: "பூளை¹ pūḷai, n. [M. pula.] 1. Red silk-cotton. See இலவு¹. 2. Wool plant, aerua; 3. Javanese wool plant, m. sh., Aerua javanica; 4. Flower worn as a symbol of victory" — generic for the genus in sense 2, but the only species gloss is Aerva javanica. Aerva lanata has its own headword, p.1463: "சிறுபூளை ciṟu-pūḷai, n. Aerua lanata", with a Cilappatikāram 9.43 citation. Both independent sources for this species agree: API Vol V, monograph PATTŪRA (Whole Plant), Sanskrit: Gorakṣagañja, Bhadrā, Tamil: Cherupoolai; Pandanus record for Aerva lanata, Tamil: ceṟupūḷai. The qualifier சிறு- is what distinguishes the species, so dropping it changes the referent.

rejected.name: नागरङ्गफलम्
rejected.denotesInstead: Citrus aurantium (bitter/Seville orange)
rejected.reason: This is a genuine Sanskrit plant name, but for the wrong species. Every lexicon I retrieved assigns नागरङ्ग to the orange (Citrus aurantium / C. sinensis), not to the citron. The Sanskrit for Citrus medica is बीजपूर (Apte: 'the citron tree'; Bhojanakutūhala, 17th c.) and मातुलुङ्ग (Apte: 'a kind of citron tree'). Leaving नागरङ्गफलम् on a Citrus medica monograph would put the orange's name on the citron.

rejected.name: நாரத்தம்பழம்
rejected.denotesInstead: Citrus aurantium (orange / Seville orange) in the University of Madras Tamil Lexicon
rejected.reason: The நாரத்தை family of names is a floating Citrus label: CRC World Dictionary (via wisdomlib) attaches 'Narattai' to Atalantia monophylla, Citrus aurantifolia, Citrus aurantium AND Citrus medica, while the Tamil Lexicon, the stronger authority, lists only oranges and wild lime. Modern Tamil Nadu pickle usage (நார்த்தங்காய்) does sometimes mean citron, which is exactly why this name cannot be presented as the Tamil for Citrus medica without misleading. Not confirmed; the lexicon's primary referent is a different species.

rejected.name: अश्वत्थः
rejected.denotesInstead: Ficus religiosa (peepal / bodhi tree)
rejected.reason: This is the seeded Wikidata error. अश्वत्थ is unambiguously Ficus religiosa in every Sanskrit lexicon and classical Ayurvedic source I retrieved, and Ficus religiosa is in a different family (Moraceae) from Aegle marmelos (Rutaceae). It must be dropped from this page.

rejected.name: अश्वत्थः
rejected.denotesInstead: Ficus religiosa (peepal / bodhi tree)
rejected.reason: The seeded Wikidata error, repeated on this page. अश्वत्थ is Ficus religiosa (Moraceae), not Aegle marmelos (Rutaceae). Drop it.

rejected.name: अश्वत्थः
rejected.denotesInstead: Ficus religiosa (peepal / bodhi tree)
rejected.reason: The seeded Wikidata error, third occurrence on an Aegle marmelos page. Especially dangerous here: both Ficus religiosa leaves and bilva leaves are ritual offerings, so an aśvattha gloss on a bilva-patra page would read plausibly and still be wrong. Drop it.

rejected.name: ब्रम्हमाण्डुकी
rejected.denotesInstead: Centella asiatica (mandukaparni / gotu kola)
rejected.reason: A second genuine misidentification in this batch. ब्रह्ममण्डूकी / ब्रह्ममण्डूक belongs to the मण्डूकपर्णी group, which is Centella asiatica (Apiaceae), not Bacopa monnieri (Plantaginaceae). The confusion is old and well documented: 'brahmi' was conflated with mandukaparni from about the 16th century, which is exactly why a mandukaparni-derived name must not sit on a Bacopa page. None of the Hindi lists I retrieved for Bacopa ('Names of Plants in India': बाम, ब्राह्मी, जलबूटी, जलनीम, नीरब्राह्मी, सफेद चमनी) contains it.

rejected.name: अश्वत्थः
rejected.denotesInstead: Ficus religiosa (peepal / bodhi tree)
rejected.reason: The seeded Wikidata error again, here on a Bacopa page. अश्वत्थ is a large fig tree; Bacopa monnieri is a creeping aquatic herb. Nothing connects them. Drop it.

rejected.name: अश्वत्थः
rejected.denotesInstead: Ficus religiosa (peepal / bodhi tree)
rejected.reason: The seeded Wikidata error, fourth occurrence in this batch. अश्वत्थ is Ficus religiosa (Moraceae); Santalum album is Santalaceae. The extensive Sanskrit synonym list for sandalwood in 'Names of Plants in India' (चन्दनम्, श्रीखण्ड, गन्धसार, मलयज, पटीर, हरिगन्ध and many more) contains nothing of the sort. Drop it.

rejected.name: மரமஞ்சள்
rejected.denotesInstead: Coscinium fenestratum (Goetgh.) Colebr. (Menispermaceae), the South Indian climber 'tree turmeric'
rejected.reason: THIS IS THE BATCH'S aśvattha-CLASS ERROR. The University of Madras Tamil Lexicon (via agarathi.com) defines மரமஞ்சள் as 'Tree turmeric, s. cl., Coscinium fenestratum; கொடிவகை' — a climber, not a Berberis shrub; the Tamil Tamil Akaramuthali likewise glosses it 'ஒருகொடிவகை' (a kind of climber). Tamil names given for Berberis aristata by botanical sources are entirely different: mullukala, usikkala, kasturimanjal (India Biodiversity / PMC3566491). The reason this error propagates is market substitution: in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, Coscinium fenestratum stem is traded AS Daruharidra, and the Daruharidra market-sample study (PMC3566491) is specifically about that adulteration. English Wikipedia repeats 'Mara manjal' in the Berberis aristata lead and Wikidata harvests it from there, so this candidate has a mirror, not a corroborator. Carrying it would print the name of a different family's plant on a Berberis page.

rejected.name: பெருஞ்சீரகம்
rejected.denotesInstead: Pimpinella anisum (common anise), and secondarily Illicium anisatum (star/Chinese anise), per the Madras Tamil Lexicon and DSAL
rejected.reason: The sources split. API Part I Vol I (MIŚREYĀ, Foeniculum vulgare) gives Tamil = Shombu (சோம்பு) and assigns the perum-jeeragam type name to Malayalam ('Parinjaeragum'). The Madras Tamil Lexicon and DSAL define பெருஞ்சீரகம் as '1. Common anise, Pimpinella anisum; 2. Chinese anise, Illicium anisatum'. Only Winslow equates it with fennel ('Anise seed, sweet fennel, சோம்பு. Anethum Foeniculum'). Modern Tamil Nadu market usage does mean fennel by it, but with the pharmacopoeia and the standard lexicon pointing to சோம்பு and Pimpinella anisum respectively, this fails the independent-attestation test for Foeniculum vulgare.

rejected.name: பெருஞ்சீரகம்
rejected.denotesInstead: Pimpinella anisum (common anise), and secondarily Illicium anisatum, per the Madras Tamil Lexicon and DSAL
rejected.reason: API Part I Vol I gives Tamil சோம்பு for Foeniculum vulgare and puts the perum-jeeragam form under Malayalam; the Madras Tamil Lexicon/DSAL gloss பெருஞ்சீரகம் as anise (Pimpinella anisum / Illicium anisatum). Winslow alone equates it with sweet fennel. Ambiguous in the sources, so not confirmed for this species.

rejected.name: अश्वत्थः
rejected.denotesInstead: Ficus religiosa (the pipal / bo-tree)
rejected.reason: This is the planted error and it is a real botanical error, not merely an unattested string. wisdomlib s.v. Aśvattha, citing Sanskrit lexicons, Dharmaśāstra, Śaivism and Ayurveda/Rasaśāstra sources, identifies अश्वत्थ unanimously as Ficus religiosa L. (Moraceae), another name for Pippala. API Part I Vol I's Sanskrit synonyms for HARĪTAKĪ are Abhayā, Kāyasthā, Śivā, Pathyā, Vijayā — अश्वत्थः is absent, as it is from every nighantu synonym list for Terminalia chebula I retrieved. The same bogus alias is attached to Adhatoda vasica and Aegle marmelos in this dataset, confirming it is a Wikidata alias contamination. It must be removed, and it would mislead a reader badly if left: Ficus religiosa is a different family and a different drug.

rejected.name: செங்கரும்பு
rejected.denotesInstead: the red-caned cultivar of sugarcane specifically ('செந்நிறமுள்ள கரும்புவகை'), not Saccharum officinarum as a species
rejected.reason: Madras Tamil Lexicon, Fabricius, Winslow and DSAL all gloss செங்கரும்பு narrowly as 'Red sugar-cane; செந்நிறமுள்ள கரும்புவகை' — a colour variety, செம் (red) + கரும்பு. The species-level Tamil name is கரும்பு: API Part I Vol II, monograph 22 IKṢU (dried stem of Saccharum officinarum Linn.) gives Tamil: Karumbu, and Flowers of India gives 'Tamil: கரும்பு (Karumbu), புண்டறம் (Pundaram)'. Publishing செங்கரும்பு as the Tamil name of the Ikshu drug would misstate it as a cultivar name.

rejected.name: குமட்டிக்காய்
rejected.denotesInstead: the unqualified கொம்மட்டி / குமட்டி denotes a small watermelon (Citrullus, i.e. C. lanatus) and Cucumis trigonus per DSAL; Citrullus colocynthis is distinguished in Tamil by the பேய்- prefix (பேய்த்தும்மட்டி / பேய்க்கொம்மட்டி)
rejected.reason: Not attested for this species. API Part I Vol III, monograph 30 INDRAVĀRUṆĪ gives Tamil: Peitummatti (and Telugu Peikummatti); Flowers of India gives Tamil 'kumatti, pey-komatti'. The Tamil dictionaries make the distinction explicit: DSAL s.v. கொம்மட்டி = 'A small water-melon, climber, Citrullus' and 'Country cucumber, climber, Cucumis trigonus; தும்மட்டி', while குமட்டிக்காய் appears only in Na Kadirvelu Pillai's dictionary glossed as 'ஆற்றுத்தும்முட்டிக்காய்' with no species. Published as the Tamil name of the colocynth drug it would point a reader at watermelon or Cucumis trigonus.

rejected.name: மௌவல்
rejected.denotesInstead: Jasminum spp. generally — the lexicon gloss is 'wild jasmine' (வனமல்லிகை / காட்டுமல்லிகை), with cross-references to Arabian jasmine (Jasminum sambac) and to wild jasmine (Jasminum angustifolium); no authority pins it to Jasminum officinale
rejected.reason: I retrieved the Tamil Lexicon entry itself (dt.madurai.io, Madras University Tamil Lexicon, corroborated by Agarathi via Wiktionary). It defines மௌவல் only as 'the wild jasmine, வனமல்லிகை', cross-referenced to காட்டுமல்லிகை and, in classical usage, also to Arabian jasmine and even to the lotus. The lexicon does not assign it to a species, and the species mappings circulating online split it across Jasminum officinale, J. grandiflorum and J. angustifolium. That is a genus-level word being presented as a species name, so confirmed stays false. It is also a literary/archaic word, not what a Tamil speaker would search.

rejected.name: मन्दारः
rejected.denotesInstead: Erythrina variegata (Indian coral tree) — Sanskrit मन्दार / मन्दारक / मन्दारवः, the Ayurvedic drug Paribhadra (पारिभद्रः); the word is also used in Sanskrit for the mythological coral tree and, in some lexicons, for Calotropis gigantea
rejected.reason: This is the kind of error worth stopping. IISc Flora of Peninsular India gives Sanskrit for Bauhinia variegata as 'Kanchanara' only, and the API Kanchanara monograph gives Kanchanara and Kovidara. Retrieval for मन्दार instead returns Erythrina variegata: Sanskrit names mandara, mandarakah, mandaravah, paribhadrah. The Bauhinia association comes through Dravidian, not Sanskrit — Tamil மந்தாரை, Kannada 'Kempu mandara', Telugu 'Mandari' are all genuine names for Bauhinia variegata, and Wikidata appears to have back-formed a Sanskrit label from them. Presented as Sanskrit on a Kachnar page, मन्दारः points a reader at the coral tree. Use काञ्चनारः / कोविदारः instead.

rejected.name: மலையாத்தி
rejected.denotesInstead: Bauhinia malabarica — MMPND's 'Sorting Bauhinia names' places மலையாத்தி (malai-y-atti) under Bauhinia malabarica, not B. variegata; the ஆத்தி word-family (ஆத்தி, புளியாத்தி, வரையாத்தி) belongs to Bauhinia racemosa and relatives, with aarai/aaththi cognates covering B. racemosa, B. tomentosa, B. spicata and B. parviflora
rejected.reason: A second genuine misassignment. I checked MMPND's per-species Bauhinia listing directly: under B. variegata it gives only Hindi 'Kachnar' and no Tamil name, while மலையாத்தி appears under Bauhinia malabarica; Flowers of India associates malaiyatti and புளியாத்தி with Bauhinia racemosa. IISc Flora of Peninsular India gives the Tamil for B. variegata as 'Sigappumanch, Sigappumantharai' (சிகப்பு மந்தாரை / செம்மந்தாரை). So மலையாத்தி is a real Tamil plant name for a different Bauhinia and would mislead a reader on this page.

rejected.name: हरिद्र
rejected.denotesInstead: Curcuma longa — हरिद्रा is turmeric, one of the most fixed plant names in Sanskrit and Hindi. The near-homograph हरिद्रु is identified by Monier-Williams with Curcuma aromatica and 'a sort of Pinus', and in Indian usage with Haldina cordifolia (Hindi हल्दू, formerly Adina cordifolia) — a different Rubiaceae tree that is also sometimes called कदम्बु in Tamil. None of these is Neolamarckia cadamba.
rejected.reason: A real botanical error, not merely an unattested string. I retrieved the haridru/haridra entry on wisdomlib: the identifications are Curcuma aromatica, Pinus spp., Chloroxylon swietenia and Haldina cordifolia, and kadamba is explicitly not among them. Searching Neolamarckia cadamba's own vernacular lists (efloraofindia, Names of Plants in India) returns Sanskrit हरिप्रिय and कदम्ब, never हरिद्र. The likeliest path is confusion of हरिप्रिय with हरिद्र, or of kadamba with हल्दू / Haldina cordifolia. Left on the page, a reader sees turmeric listed as a name for a forest tree.

rejected.name: अश्वत्थः
rejected.denotesInstead: Ficus religiosa — aśvattha is the pipal/bodhi tree, one of the most unambiguous plant names in the entire Sanskrit corpus (Ṛgveda onward, Bhagavad-gītā 15.1, and every nighantu). It has no connection to Neolamarckia cadamba.
rejected.reason: This is the planted error, and it is the same Wikidata defect flagged in the brief, where अश्वत्थः is also attached to Adhatoda vasica and Aegle marmelos. No source for Neolamarckia cadamba contains it: efloraofindia and Names of Plants in India give Sanskrit हरिप्रिय and कदम्ब; Rāja Nighaṇṭu gives Kadamba, Nīpa, Dhārākadamba, Kādambarya. Must be removed — a reader would take Ficus religiosa and Neolamarckia cadamba to be the same tree.

rejected.name: கடம்பு மரம்
rejected.denotesInstead: ambiguous in Tamil — bare கடம்பு is applied to at least four species: Neolamarckia cadamba, Mitragyna parvifolia, Haldina cordifolia and Barringtonia acutangula, three of which occur around Madurai, where the Sangam-literature கடம்பு is commonly identified as Mitragyna parvifolia
rejected.reason: The species-specific Tamil name I retrieved is வெள்ளைக் கடம்பு / வெண்கடம்பு ('white kadambu') — Names of Plants in India gives வெள்ளை கதம்பு (Vellaikkatampu) for Neolamarckia cadamba, and Tamil agro-forestry sources give 'Vellai Kadambu'. The exact form கடம்பு மரம் ('kadambu tree') is not attested by any named source as a name, and dropping the qualifier வெள்ளை is precisely what makes it ambiguous across the four species above. Use வெள்ளைக் கடம்பு.

rejected.name: अश्वत्थः
rejected.denotesInstead: Ficus religiosa Linn. (the pipal/bodhi tree)
rejected.reason: This is the planted error and it is a genuine Sanskrit plant name for a completely different tree. The Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India carries its own separate monograph headed ASVATTHA (Bark), defined as 'dried bark of Ficus religiosa Linn. (Fam. Moraceae)' — api-all.txt lines 126-128 and 3132-3135 — and its Bengali/Kannada synonym slots there repeat Asvattha/Ashvattha for Ficus religiosa. Meanwhile the retrieved Sanskrit list for Andrographis paniculata (Names of Plants in India) is 'भूनिम्ब bhunimba, कालमेघ kalamegha, महातिक्ता mahatikta, यवतिक्ता yavatikta' and contains no अश्वत्थ at all. Must be dropped from this page; it is the same bad Wikidata alias that also contaminates Adhatoda vasica and Aegle marmelos.

rejected.name: मन्दारः
rejected.denotesInstead: Primarily Erythrina variegata / E. suberosa (the coral tree); also Calotropis gigantea and C. procera (arka), Piliostigma malabaricum, Ficus benjamina and Bauhinia tomentosa
rejected.reason: This is a real Sanskrit plant name but a badly ambiguous one that would mislead on a Bauhinia variegata page. API's KANCANARA monograph (Bauhinia variegata) gives Sanskrit 'Kancanaraka' only, with no Mandara anywhere. Within the genus, API attaches the mandara word-family to a different species: its PITA-KANCANARA monograph (Bauhinia racemosa Lamk., api-all.txt line 101405 ff.) lists Kannada 'Kadu manthara, ... Mandara', Malayalam 'Mandarum' and Tamil 'Malai-mandarai'. The lexicon compilation at wisdomlib.org/definition/mandara resolves mandāra chiefly to Erythrina suberosa, Erythrina variegata, Calotropis procera and C. gigantea, with Bauhinia variegata appearing only as a secondary identification. The Sanskrit name for this species is काञ्चनारः (API monograph title), which I report in `discovered`. Drop मन्दारः.

rejected.name: மலையாத்தி
rejected.denotesInstead: Bauhinia racemosa Lamk. per the Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India; Bauhinia malabarica Roxb. per MMPND
rejected.reason: Species-level error. API's PITA-KANCANARA monograph, which is explicitly Bauhinia racemosa Lamk., lists Tamil 'Atthi, Malai-atti, Malai-mandarai' — so the official source assigns Malai-atti (மலையாத்தி) to B. racemosa, not B. variegata. The Multilingual Multiscript Plant Name Database (Univ. of Melbourne, plantnames.unimelb.edu.au/Sorting/Bauhinia.html) assigns 'மலையாத்தி Malaiyatti' to Bauhinia malabarica Roxb. and gives no Tamil name at all for B. variegata. API's Tamil for B. variegata is 'Sigappu mandarai, Sihappu mantarai' (செம்மந்தாரை). Names of Plants in India does list மலையாத்தி under B. variegata, but it is outvoted by two sources that place it on other Bauhinia species, and on a reference page it would send a reader to the wrong tree.

rejected.name: कचनार
rejected.denotesInstead: Bauhinia variegata
rejected.reason: This is the error type you flagged. efloraofindia's Bauhinia variegata page gives Hindi "कचनार kachnar, कचनाल kachnal" — bare कचनार is B. variegata, the common kachnar of markets and of the Ayurvedic drug Kanchanara. For Bauhinia purpurea, efloraofindia and IMPPAT give Hindi कांचन (kanchan), लाल कचनार (lal kachnar) and केवनार (kevnar): the purple species is distinguished by the qualifier लाल/रक्त. Putting unqualified कचनार on a B. purpurea page asserts the wrong species.

rejected.name: कोविदार
rejected.denotesInstead: Bauhinia variegata
rejected.reason: Two faults. (1) Species: efloraofindia lists कोविदार / कोविदारः among the Sanskrit names of Bauhinia variegata (alongside काञ्चनार kanchanara), while for Bauhinia purpurea it and IMPPAT give Sanskrit रक्तकोविदार (rakta-kovidara) and रक्तकांचन — the purple species carries the रक्त qualifier, so bare कोविदार points at B. variegata. (2) Language: कोविदार is a Sanskrit term (efloraofindia also records it as Marathi), not a Hindi vernacular name, so the hi label is wrong even where the word is right. If the monograph is to stay on B. purpurea, the defensible Sanskrit form is रक्तकोविदार.

rejected.name: 12.தோழிக்குரைத்த பத்து
rejected.denotesInstead: Nothing botanical. It is a Tamil literary section heading (Ainkuṟunūṟu, decad 12, 'tōḻikkuraitta pattu'), not a species name.
rejected.reason: This is not a plant name at all. It is the heading of decad 12 of Ainkuṟunūṟu, a Sangam-era Tamil anthology in the Eṭṭuttokai, meaning 'the ten (songs) spoken to the confidante' (tamilsurangam.in literature index; Ainkurunuru). The leading '12.' is a table-of-contents number, which is the tell. It has been harvested into a vernacular-name slot by mistake. API gives Tamil "Malaivembu" and MMPND gives "மலை வேம்பு Malai vembu, காட்டு வேம்பூ Kattu vembhu" for Melia azedarach. Reject outright.

rejected.name: रुबिया  कॉर्डिफ़ोलिया
rejected.denotesInstead: Nothing. It is the Latin binomial transliterated into Devanagari, not a vernacular name.
rejected.reason: This is not a Hindi plant name. It is the Latin binomial 'Rubia cordifolia' respelled in Devanagari, double space and all, which is how Wikidata stores script-transliterated labels. API's MANJISTHA monograph gives Hindi "Manjitha, Manjit"; MMPND gives Hindi "Majith, Manjit". No Hindi source calls the plant रुबिया कॉर्डिफ़ोलिया. Reject; the real Hindi name is मंजीठ.

rejected.name: रुबिअ कोर्दिफ़्ओलिअ
rejected.denotesInstead: Nothing. It is the Latin binomial transliterated into Devanagari, not a Sanskrit name.
rejected.reason: Same failure as the Hindi entry: a Devanagari transliteration of 'Rubia cordifolia', and a worse one (the broken cluster फ़्ओ is not valid Devanagari orthography). API's Sanskrit synonyms for Rubia cordifolia are "Yojnavalli, Vastrarajini, Rakta"; MMPND gives "Gandari, Manjishta, Manjishtha, Manjistha, Munjistha". Reject; the real Sanskrit name is मञ्जिष्ठा.

rejected.name: रुबिया  कॉर्डिफ़ोलिया
rejected.denotesInstead: Nothing. It is the Latin binomial transliterated into Devanagari, not a vernacular name.
rejected.reason: Identical duplicate of the manjishtha candidate: the Latin binomial in Devanagari, not a Hindi name. API MANJISTHA monograph gives Hindi "Manjitha, Manjit"; MMPND gives "Majith, Manjit". Reject.

rejected.name: रुबिअ कोर्दिफ़्ओलिअ
rejected.denotesInstead: Nothing. It is the Latin binomial transliterated into Devanagari, not a Sanskrit name.
rejected.reason: Identical duplicate of the manjishtha candidate: the Latin binomial in Devanagari with an invalid consonant cluster. Not attested as Sanskrit by API or MMPND. Reject.

rejected.name: नागरङ्गफलम्
rejected.denotesInstead: Citrus × aurantium / Citrus × sinensis, the orange. Not Citrus medica.
rejected.reason: WRONG SPECIES. नागरङ्ग is the Sanskrit name of the orange, not the citron. Wisdomlib's Sanskrit plant-name entry identifies Nāgaraṅga with Citrus aurantium L. (synonyms Citrus sinensis, Citrus vulgaris) and notes that English 'orange' derives from it via Arabic nāranj. API's BIJAPURA monograph on Citrus medica gives Sanskrit "Matulunga", and MMPND's Sanskrit line for Citrus medica is "अम्‍लकेसर, बीजाण्‍ड, जम्भीर, लुंग, महाफल, मातुलुङ्ग, पूरक, रुचक, सुमनःफल" with no नागरङ्ग anywhere. This is exactly the kind of genuine-name-wrong-plant error that would survive on the page, so flag and drop. (One 17th-c. dietetics text, Bhojanakutūhala, glosses nāgaraṅga loosely as 'citron', but that is a minority reading against API and MMPND.)

rejected.name: நாரத்தம்பழம்
rejected.denotesInstead: Citrus × aurantium, the bitter/sour orange (narthangai). Not Citrus medica.
rejected.reason: WRONG SPECIES. MMPND's Citrus sorting pages place "நாரந்தை Nārantai, நரந்தம்பழம் Narantampaḻam" exclusively under Citrus × aurantium (bitter orange, the narthangai pickled in Tamil cooking), and MMPND's Citrus medica Tamil line is "Campalam, Campiram, எலுமிச்சை Elumiccai, கடரநாரத்தை Kaṭāranārattai, கொம்மட்டிமாதுளை Kommatti-matulai". API's BIJAPURA monograph gives Tamil "Turunji Pazham, Kadarangai" for Citrus medica. The Citrus medica Tamil name is the qualified compound கடாரநாரத்தை or துருஞ்சிப்பழம்; bare நாரத்தம்பழம் is the bitter orange. Drop and flag.

rejected.name: கார்டினியா கம்மிபெரா
rejected.denotesInstead: Nothing. It is the Latin binomial transliterated into Tamil script, not a vernacular name.
rejected.reason: Not a Tamil plant name. It is the Latin binomial 'Gardenia gummifera' respelled in Tamil script, the same Wikidata script-transliteration artefact as the Rubia entries. API's NADIHINGU (Exudate) monograph on Gardenia gummifera gives Tamil "Tikka malli" (Hindi "Naadihingu, Dikaamaali", Sanskrit "Hingunadika"), and flowersofindia's Gummy Gardenia entry gives Tamil kambil, sirukkambil, tikkamalli. Reject; the real Tamil name is திக்கமல்லி.

rejected.name: अश्वत्थः
rejected.denotesInstead: Ficus religiosa
rejected.reason: The retrieved Sanskrit list for Azadirachta indica (efloraofindia: निम्ब, अरिष्ट, पिचुमन्द, पारिभद्र, वरतिक्त, यवनेष्ट and ~20 more) contains no अश्वत्थ. I then retrieved the Ficus religiosa page on the same source, which lists अश्वत्थ as its leading Sanskrit name (Hindi पीपल). अश्वत्थ is Ficus religiosa, not neem. This is the seeded Wikidata error.

rejected.name: अश्वत्थः
rejected.denotesInstead: Ficus religiosa
rejected.reason: Absent from the retrieved Sanskrit list for Azadirachta indica (efloraofindia). The same source's Ficus religiosa page lists अश्वत्थ as its principal Sanskrit name. Wrong species; must be dropped.

rejected.name: अश्वत्थः
rejected.denotesInstead: Ficus religiosa
rejected.reason: Not in the retrieved Sanskrit list for Azadirachta indica; efloraofindia attests अश्वत्थ for Ficus religiosa. Wrong species.

rejected.name: अश्वत्थः
rejected.denotesInstead: Ficus religiosa
rejected.reason: Not in the retrieved Sanskrit list for Azadirachta indica; efloraofindia attests अश्वत्थ for Ficus religiosa. Wrong species.

rejected.name: பசலை கீரை
rejected.denotesInstead: Basella alba (Malabar spinach)
rejected.reason: Flowers of India gives the Tamil names of Spinacia oleracea as "Vachalaikkirai, Vasaiyilaikkirai" and does not list pasalai keerai; efloraofindia's Basella alba page lists Tamil "Pasalai keerai" and "Vasalakkirai" for THAT species. பசலை/பசலைக்கீரை is the Tamil name of Basella alba, a Basellaceae vine, not of true spinach, which is not a traditional Tamil green. This is a genuine cross-species misattribution of the kind that would survive on the page.

rejected.name: புளிமா
rejected.denotesInstead: Buchanania axillaris (Buchanan's mango); the same Tamil word is also applied to Spondias pinnata (Indian hog-plum) and Averrhoa bilimbi
rejected.reason: Retrieved University of Madras Tamil Lexicon (via agarathi.com) for புளிமா: 'a species of mango, sour in taste', 'bilimbi tree', 'Buchanan's mango', 'Indian hog-plum (Spondias mangifera)'. It is a genuine Tamil plant name but not for Buchanania lanzan: eFloraofIndia gives Tamil சாரம் / காட்டுமா for B. lanzan and API gives Tamil 'Saarapparuppu'. Buchanania axillaris is the sister species, so this would sit on the page as a plausible-looking misidentification.

rejected.name: अश्वत्थः
rejected.denotesInstead: Ficus religiosa
rejected.reason: This is the seeded error. Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I, monograph 11, is ASVATTHA (Bark) = Ficus religiosa Linn., with Sanskrit synonym Pippala, Hindi 'Pipala, Pipal', Tamil 'Arasamaram, Arasu'. अश्वत्थ is the pipal, a Moraceae tree, and has no relation to Areca catechu, a palm. API's Sanskrit synonyms for Areca are Kramuka, Ghonta and the monograph name Puga. Must not go on this page.

rejected.name: பாலை
rejected.denotesInstead: Manilkara kauki (Mimusops kauki); bare பாலை is also the generic Tamil tree element used for Wrightia tinctoria (வெட்பாலை), Alstonia scholaris (ஏழிலைப்பாலை) and Periploca esculenta (ஊசிப்பாலை)
rejected.reason: Retrieved University of Madras Tamil Lexicon (via agarathi.com) for பாலை: 'Silvery-leaved ape-flower, m. tr., Mimusops kauki', and Winslow's Tamil-English Dictionary, which records பாலை only inside compounds for Periploca esculenta, Echites scholaris (= Alstonia scholaris), Gelonium bifarium, Asclepias volubilis and Nerium antidysentericum (= Wrightia). eFloraofIndia's Tamil for Manilkara hexandra is உலக்கைப்பாலை, not bare பாலை. So the harvested form resolves to a different Manilkara species in the lexicon and is otherwise a floating generic element, which on a monograph page reads as a precise name for this species when it is not.

rejected.name: क्षीरिणीसस्यम्
rejected.denotesInstead: Manilkara hexandra (its head word क्षीरिणी is the attested Sanskrit for that species); क्षीरिणी is also a recorded Sanskrit synonym of Dugdhika/Euphorbia
rejected.reason: Retrieved API's SVETA SARIVA monograph, whose Sanskrit synonyms for Hemidesmus indicus are Ananta, Gopasuta and Sariva. The compound क्षीरिणीसस्यम् ('kṣīriṇī-crop') appears in no pharmacopoeia or lexicon I retrieved for this species, and its shape suggests a constructed Wikidata-era coinage rather than a nighantu name. Its head word is independently attested elsewhere: eFloraofIndia gives Sanskrit क्षीरिणी for Manilkara hexandra, and API lists Ksirini among the Sanskrit synonyms of Dugdhika (Euphorbia). Hemidesmus is latex-bearing, which is probably how the confusion arose, but the name points away from it.

rejected.name: अश्वत्थः
rejected.denotesInstead: Ficus religiosa
rejected.reason: The seeded error again, on a second page. API Part I monograph 11 is ASVATTHA (Bark) = Ficus religiosa Linn., Sanskrit synonym Pippala, Hindi 'Pipala, Pipal', Tamil 'Arasamaram, Arasu'. Rauvolfia serpentina is an Apocynaceae undershrub; अश्वत्थ is the pipal fig. API's Sanskrit synonyms for this species are Nakuli, Candrika and Chandramarah. That the same wrong alias was attached to Adhatoda vasica, Aegle marmelos, Areca catechu and Rauvolfia serpentina shows it is a systematic Wikidata defect, not a one-off: every page in the dataset carrying अश्वत्थः should be swept, not just these.

rejected.name: கோங்கு
rejected.denotesInstead: Cochlospermum religiosum (yellow silk cotton tree) — கோங்கு / கோங்கம்
rejected.reason: This is the aśvattha-type error in this batch. Two independent sources list the Tamil names of Bombax ceiba and neither includes கோங்கு: efloraofindia gives Tamil இலவு (ilavu), முள்ளிலவு (mullilavu), பூலா (puulaa); India Flora Online (IISc) gives Tamil 'Ilavu, Purani'. Meanwhile கோங்கு is a real and well-documented Tamil tree name belonging to a different species: Tamil Wikipedia's கோங்கம் article and Sangam-literature commentary identify கோங்கம்/கோங்கு as Cochlospermum religiosum, the yellow silk cotton tree. The confusion is plausible (both are called 'silk cotton'), which is exactly why it would survive on a page. Drop it.

rejected.name: மூவிலை
rejected.denotesInstead: Pseudarthria viscida (Moovila / மூவிலை), the trifoliate Dasamula drug used in South India as a substitute for Shalaparni
rejected.reason: efloraofindia's Desmodium gangeticum page gives only one Tamil name, புள்ளடி (pullati); Kerala SMPB's monograph gives Tamil/Malayalam Orila (ഓരില, 'one leaf'), which is the diagnostic name for D. gangeticum because its leaf is unifoliate. மூவிலை means 'three leaves' and is the established name of Pseudarthria viscida: wisdomlib's botanical definition of 'Moovila' resolves it to Pseudarthria viscida, Malayalam muvila, Tamil 'moovilai pachilai'. Literature on Dasamula adulteration treats Pseudarthria viscida (Moovila) explicitly as the South Indian substitute for Desmodium gangeticum (Orila), so some compilations do carry Moovilai under D. gangeticum — that is the substitution error propagating, not an independent attestation. Keep it off the page.

rejected.name: जटामांसी
rejected.denotesInstead: Nardostachys jatamansi (true Jatamansi / spikenard), a separate API monograph drug
rejected.reason: Second real cross-species error in this batch. जटामांसी is the Hindi/Sanskrit name of Nardostachys jatamansi, which has its own Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia monograph distinct from Tagara. For Valeriana jatamansi, efloraofindia records the Indian trade names as 'Nihani / Mushkbala / Tagar' — not Jatamansi — and review literature on Tagara (IJAPR, 'Pharmacological Actions of Valeriana wallichii (Tagara)') gives Hindi Tagar / Sugandhabala / Mushkbala. The two Himalayan herbs are documented as routinely confused and cross-adulterated in trade precisely because the species epithet of Valeriana jatamansi repeats the other plant's name; that is how this label reached Wikidata. Putting जटामांसी on a Tagara page would misidentify the drug. Correct Hindi forms are in discovered.

rejected.name: वामनी
rejected.denotesInstead: Gossypium herbaceum (cotton plant)
rejected.reason: This is a genuine plant name for the wrong plant, the same failure class as the aśvattha error. wisdomlib's entry for Vamani/Vāmanī records: 'Vamani in India is the name of a plant defined with Gossypium herbaceum in various botanical sources' (synonym Gossypium prostratum), and the Tamil lexicon entry glosses it 'Cotton plant; பருத்திச் செடி'. Monier-Williams likewise gives 'the cotton shrub' for वामनी. Separately I retrieved the Vacha synonym set for Acorus calamus from MMPND (Sanskrit: Vacha, Bhuta nashini), Flowers of India (वचा Vachaa, वाच Vacha, Bhadra) and the Vacha dravyaguna literature (Ugragandha, Golomi, Lomashi, Jatila, Shadgrantha/Shataparvika, Hemavati, Khadiravacha) and वामनी appears in none of them; MMPND and Flowers of India were checked explicitly for it and do not list it. Must be removed: left on the page it would assert that a cotton name is an Acorus name.

rejected.name: மூங்கிலிரிசி
rejected.denotesInstead: Not a species name: it denotes bamboo rice, the edible seed/grain produced by bamboo at flowering (மூங்கில் அரிசி), a plant part rather than the plant
rejected.reason: Retrieved the Tamil name set for Bambusa bambos from Flowers of India ('Tamil: குழாய்மூங்கில் kulay-munkil, பெருமூங்கில் peru-munkil') and MMPND Sorting Bambusa names under Bambusa arundinacea ('Tamil: Mullumangila, Mulmunkil, Mungil'). Both were checked explicitly for மூங்கிலிரிசி / 'moongil arisi' and neither lists it. The string is மூங்கில் + அரிசி, literally 'bamboo rice', the seed harvested when bamboo masses-flowers. So it is a real Tamil word tied to bamboo, but it names a product, not the species, and a reader would take it for the plant's Tamil name. Use மூங்கில் or முள்மூங்கில் instead. Relatedly, the Ayurvedic drug behind the slug Vamsha is usually वंशलोचन (tabasheer, the siliceous culm exudate), another part rather than the plant, so this page needs its plant-versus-part distinction made explicit.

rejected.name: अश्वत्थः
rejected.denotesInstead: Ficus religiosa (the sacred fig / peepal)
rejected.reason: This is the planted error and it is a real botanical error. Retrieved from both directions. Positively: MMPND Sorting Ficus names lists under Ficus religiosa 'Sanskrit: Ashvatha, Asvattha, Ashvathha, Aswattha, Bodhidruma, Bodhivrska, Pippala, Shuchidruma, Yajnika' and 'Hindi: पीपल Pipal'; wisdomlib's Ashvattha entry and the Ashvattha dravyaguna monographs identify अश्वत्थ as Ficus religiosa, classed by Caraka in the Kaṣāya mahākaṣāya group. Negatively: MMPND's full Sanskrit list for Justicia adhatoda (Adusa, Arusha, Atrusha, Bhishangamata, Kaphahari, Simhamukhi, Simhi, Simhika, Sinhaparni, Shwetavasa, Vasa, Vasaka, Vasika) contains no form of aśvattha, and neither does the Bhāvaprakāśa synonym set for Vāsā reported in the Adhatoda reviews. Aśvattha and Vāsā are not even in the same family (Moraceae vs Acanthaceae). Must be deleted from this page.

rejected.name: बादाम का पेड
rejected.denotesInstead: Prunus dulcis (sweet almond). The page's stated botanical is the genus Prunus (Q39918), which is broader than any of these names
rejected.reason: Two separate problems. First, the string is not a name but a descriptive noun phrase: बादाम का पेड़ means 'the almond tree'. Flowers of India's Almond page gives 'Hindi: बादाम Badam, बदाम' and no source I retrieved gives the phrase as a vernacular name; it is the kind of gloss Wikidata stores as a label. It is also missing the nukta on ड़ (पेड़, not पेड). Second, and more consequential for the page: all three candidates here name the almond, Prunus dulcis, while the page's botanical field is the bare genus Prunus, which also contains plums, cherries, peaches and apricots. Presenting almond names against the genus would tell a reader that बादाम denotes Prunus generally, which is false. Set this page's species to Prunus dulcis (Mill.) D.A.Webb and use बादाम for Hindi.

rejected.name: आमेतसवृक्षः
rejected.denotesInstead: Nothing in Ayurvedic nomenclature as spelled; the nearest real Sanskrit name, आम्लवेतसः (Amlavetasa), is Garcinia pedunculata (with Rumex vesicarius / Rheum emodi as disputed alternatives), a different API monograph
rejected.reason: This string appears in exactly one place: the Sanskrit Wikipedia article title आमेतसवृक्षः, which is a Wikidata mirror and therefore not independent corroboration. No API, nighantu or Dravyaguna source gives it. Tellingly, that same Sanskrit Wikipedia page itself calls the fruit वृक्षाम्लफलम् and the juice वृक्षाम्ल-फलरसः, i.e. it does not use its own title as the plant's name. The accepted Sanskrit name for Garcinia indica is वृक्षाम्ल / वृक्षाम्ला (eFloraofIndia, sdach.ac.in Dravyaguna monograph, API Part I Vol V monograph title Vrikshamla). आमेतसवृक्षः reads as a corruption of आम्लवेतस-वृक्षः, and Amlavetasa is a separate drug identified with Garcinia pedunculata (wisdomlib Amlavetasa entry citing Caraka-samhita; sdach.ac.in Amlavetasa monograph), so leaving it on the page would both invent a name and pull in another species. Drop it.

rejected.name: முருகல்
rejected.denotesInstead: Correct species, wrong language: this is the Kannada name (ಮುರ್ಗಿನ murgina / "murugalu mara") for Garcinia indica, not a Tamil name
rejected.reason: The University of Madras Tamil Lexicon (via agarathi.com) has no plant sense for முருகல் at all, and no Tamil-language botanical sense anywhere. eFloraofIndia's Garcinia indica page lists no Tamil name whatsoever, while giving Kannada ಮುರ್ಗಿನ (murgina) and ಪುನರ್ಪುಳಿ (punarpuli); the sdach.ac.in Dravyaguna monograph likewise lists Kannada and Malayalam but no Tamil. Garcinia indica is a Konkan/Western Ghats species with no Tamil Nadu range, consistent with there being no Tamil name. The Sanskrit Wikipedia page is the only source labelling मुरुगल् as Tamil, and on the same line it gives Kannada as "मुरुगलु मर", i.e. the same word; this looks like a Kannada name relabelled as Tamil and propagated through Wikipedia/Wikidata. Not safe to publish as Tamil.

rejected.name: ब्रम्हमाण्डुकी
rejected.denotesInstead: Centella asiatica
rejected.reason: Retrieved the term rather than guessing: wisdomlib's Brahmamanduki (ब्रह्ममण्डूकी) entry identifies it as a plant "identified with Centella asiatica (L.) Urb.", with Brahmi / Brahma-manduki / Brahamamanduki listed as that species' synonyms; the sdach.ac.in Mandukaparni monograph confirms मण्डूकपर्णी = Centella asiatica and explicitly warns that Mandukaparni is commonly confused with Brahmi (Bacopa monnieri) because Bhavaprakasha describes similar actions. The candidate's spelling (ब्रम्ह- for ब्रह्म-, -माण्डुकी for -मण्डूकी) is a nonstandard Wikidata-style orthography of that same Centella name. This is a real plant name belonging to a different species and is exactly the kind of error that would mislead a reader on a Bacopa page. Drop.

rejected.name: अश्वत्थः
rejected.denotesInstead: Ficus religiosa
rejected.reason: This is the proven error in the dataset. Retrieved the term: wisdomlib's Ashvattha entry identifies अश्वत्थ as Ficus religiosa (the holy fig / pipal, Moraceae), citing Caraka-samhita, Rajanighantu, Atharva-veda, Shatapatha-brahmana, Mahabharata and the Puranas, and records no Bacopa sense anywhere. Ashvattha is one of the least ambiguous names in Sanskrit botanical nomenclature. No API, nighantu, IMPPAT or Kerala SMPB source connects it to Bacopa monnieri. It is a genuine Sanskrit plant name for an entirely different family and would be a serious botanical error on this page. Drop, and note that the same alias is wrongly attached to Adhatoda vasica and Aegle marmelos elsewhere in this harvest, so the whole अश्वत्थः alias set from Wikidata should be treated as contaminated.

sources: Flowers of India, Pterocarpus marsupium page: 'Sanskrit: Asana, Beejaka, Petaca, Bandhukavriksha'; MMPND Sanskrit list: 'Asana, Bijaka, Bijavriksha, Priyaka, Pitasara, Mahasarja' and others

sa.name: बीजकः
sources: Flowers of India, Pterocarpus marsupium page: 'Sanskrit: Beejaka'; MMPND P. marsupium Sanskrit list: 'Bijaka, Bijavriksha'

hi.name: बीजसार
sources: MMPND Sorting Pterocarpus names, P. marsupium Hindi list: 'Bija, Bijasal, Bijasar, Bijaisaar kaashtha, Vijaisar kaashthaa'; corroborated by the Pterocarpus marsupium pharmacology reviews ('Hindi: Bijasar')

hi.name: विजयसार
sources: Flowers of India, Pterocarpus marsupium ('Indian Kino Tree') page: 'Hindi: विजयसार Vijayasara, बीज पत्ता Beeja patta, Bijasal, Bila'

ta.name: வேங்கை
sources: Flowers of India, Pterocarpus marsupium ('Indian Kino Tree') page: 'Tamil: Vengai, Accamai, Accanapann'; MMPND Sorting Pterocarpus names, P. marsupium Tamil list includes 'Vengai' and 'Udiravengai'

sa.name: अम्लबीजम्
sources: Dravyaguna Vigyan "Vrikshamla / Kokum" monograph, sdach.ac.in, which lists Amlabija among the Sanskrit synonyms for Garcinia indica alongside Raktavrikshamla, Amlapura and Amlashaka.

sa.name: वृक्षाम्ला
sources: eFloraofIndia species page for Garcinia indica, Sanskrit: वृक्षामला (vrikshamla); corroborated by the Dravyaguna Vigyan "Vrikshamla / Kokum" monograph on sdach.ac.in (Sanskrit name: Vrikshamla) and by the Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I Vol V, which titles the monograph Vrikshamla for Garcinia indica.

hi.name: कोकम
sources: Dravyaguna Vigyan monograph "Vrikshamla / Kokum" on the Ayurveda college portal sdach.ac.in lists Hindi names as "Kokum, Kokam, Komal, Amlaveta, Vishambila"; eFloraofIndia's Garcinia indica page independently records कोकम in Konkani/Gujarati script forms and English "kokam".

sa.name: ब्राह्मी
sources: Kerala State Medicinal Plants Board Bacopa monnieri page (smpbkerala.in) lists Sanskrit "Brahmi"; Rajanighantu (13th c.), via wisdomlib's Brahmi entry, treats Brahmi as a drug name with 23 synonyms (Sarasvati, Somalata, Matsyakshi, Mandukaparni-adjacent forms etc.) and modern identification with Bacopa monnieri; Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India uses Brahmi as the official Sanskrit monograph name for Bacopa monnieri.

sa.name: मत्स्याक्षी
sources: Rajanighantu (13th c.), via wisdomlib's Brahmi entry, which lists 23 synonyms of Brahmi including Matsyakshi, Sarasvati, Somalata, Medhya, Bharati and Parameshthini.

sa.name: सरस्वती
sources: Rajanighantu (13th c.), via wisdomlib's Brahmi entry, where Sarasvati heads the list of 23 synonyms for Brahmi.

hi.name: ब्राह्मी
sources: Kerala State Medicinal Plants Board species page for Bacopa monnieri (smpbkerala.in) gives Sanskrit "Brahmi", Malayalam ബ്രഹ്മി, Hindi "Barambhi", Tamil "Nirbrahmi"; IMPPAT (IIT Madras) Bacopa monnieri page gives common name "Brahmi"; Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India carries Brahmi as the official monograph name for Bacopa monnieri.

ta.name: நீர்ப்பிரமி
sources: University of Madras Tamil Lexicon (via agarathi.com) entry for நீர்ப்பிரமி: "Water hyssop, climber, Herpestis monniera". Herpestis monniera is a listed taxonomic synonym of Bacopa monnieri on the IMPPAT Bacopa monnieri page. Kerala State Medicinal Plants Board independently gives Tamil "Nirbrahmi".

sa.name: यवः
sources: wisdomlib Yava entry: Madhavacikitsa (7th c.) identifies Yava as "Hordeum vulgare L. Syn. Hordeum hexastichon L.", with further references in Ashtangasangraha (which distinguishes the anuyava and venuyava varieties) and Yogasarasangraha; ayushvedah.com carries the monograph under the drug name Yava for Hordeum vulgare.

sa.name: धान्यराजः
sources: ayushvedah.com Yava (Hordeum vulgare) monograph, Sanskrit vernacular names: "aksata, akshata, dhanyaraja, divya".

hi.name: जौ
sources: ayushvedah.com Yava (Hordeum vulgare) drug monograph, vernacular names table: Hindi "जव (jav), जौ (jau)", Sanskrit "aksata, akshata, dhanyaraja, divya", family Poaceae.

hi.name: जव
sources: ayushvedah.com Yava (Hordeum vulgare) monograph, vernacular names table, Hindi: "जव (jav), जौ (jau)".

ta.name: வாற்கோதுமை
sources: University of Madras Tamil Lexicon (via agarathi.com): "Barley cereal, Hordeum vulgare; கோதுமைவகை" (a kind of wheat-grain).

sa.name: यवानी
sources: Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India Part I Vol I carries the monograph "Yavani (Fruit)" for Trachyspermum ammi (Linn.) Sprague, and API Part II lists Yamani/Yavani as Trachyspermum ammi Fr. in compound formulations; Rajanighantu 6.38-40 (via wisdomlib) treats Yavani as the head term with fourteen synonyms.

sa.name: दीप्यकः
sources: Rajanighantu (13th c.) 6.38-40, via wisdomlib's Yavani entry, which opens the fourteen synonyms of Yavani with Dipyaka and Dipya.

sa.name: यवाग्रजः
sources: Rajanighantu (13th c.) verses 6.38-40, via wisdomlib's Yavani entry, lists fourteen synonyms of Yavani (Trachyspermum ammi) including यवाग्रज (Yavagraja), alongside दीप्यक, दीप्य, यावासाह्व, यवज, दीपनीय, उग्रगन्धा, वातारि, भूकदम्बक, दीपनी, शूलहन्त्री, यवानिका, उग्रा, तीव्रगन्धा.

sa.name: यवानिका
sources: Rajanighantu (13th c.) 6.38-40, via wisdomlib's Yavani entry, listing Yavanika among the fourteen synonyms of Yavani (Trachyspermum ammi).

hi.name: अजवाइन
sources: Hindi-language Trachyspermum ammi monograph on drvashishtsayuremedies (sites.google.com/site/drvashishtsayuremedies/ajwain-trachyspermum-ammi): "अजवायन को हिंदी में अजवाइन, ज़वेन कहा जाता है ... इसका वानस्पतिक नाम ट्रकीस्पर्मम् ऐम्मी (Trachyspermum ammi) है"; the Tata 1mg Hindi monograph uses the same spelling.

ta.name: ஓமம்
sources: University of Madras Tamil Lexicon (via agarathi.com) entry for ஓமம்: "Bishop's-weed, herbaceous plant, Carum copticum", with J. P. Fabricius and Winslow's Tamil-English dictionaries giving the same sense. Carum copticum is a listed taxonomic synonym of Trachyspermum ammi on the IMPPAT Trachyspermum ammi page.

sa.name: यूथिका
sources: eFloraofIndia species page for Jasminum auriculatum, Sanskrit: यूथिका (Yuthika), also given as Juthika.

hi.name: जूही
sources: eFloraofIndia species page for Jasminum auriculatum lists Hindi जूही (Juhi), alongside Sanskrit यूथिका (Yuthika), Tamil உச்சி மல்லிகை, Bengali যুথি/জুঁই, Marathi Jai/Jui, Telugu Adavimalle, Kannada Sanna mallige, Malayalam Sucimulla.

ta.name: உச்சி மல்லிகை
sources: eFloraofIndia species page for Jasminum auriculatum, Tamil: உச்சி மல்லிகை (Uccimalligai), also transliterated Usimalligai; the page distinguishes this from Jathi malli, which is Jasminum grandiflorum.

ta.name: முல்லை
sources: eFloraofIndia species page for Jasminum auriculatum, which states that J. auriculatum "is referred to as Mullai in Tamil" while J. grandiflorum is Jathi Malli.
